materials.name: EUROFER97 (EUROFER97-3 heat specification)
materials.nominal_choice_note: Majors at spec midpoints (Mn 0.40, C 0.105, N 0.030, W 1.10, Ta 0.12). For trace elements offer two modes: 'typical' = measured KIT analysis of EUROFER97-3 (Co 20 ppm, Ni 99 ppm, Cu 15 ppm, Mo 21 ppm, Nb <4 ppm, B 4 ppm, Al 15 ppm) and 'spec-max' = the specification limits. Activation of Co/Nb/Mo/Ni/Cu is dominated by these, so spec-max is the conservative default if the user does not know the heat. The specification does NOT limit Ag, Eu or Tb; no value available.

source.citation: V. Chakin, C. Bonnekoh, R. Gaisin, R. Ziegler, M. Duerrschnabel, M. Klimenkov, B. Gorr, M. Rieth, 'Charpy impact properties of EUROFER97-3 after neutron irradiation at 330 C and 540 C to damage doses of 21-23 dpa', Nuclear Materials and Energy 46 (2026) 102079, DOI 10.1016/j.nme.2026.102079
source.table: Table 3 'Chemical composition of EUROFER97-3 steel in wt.%' (columns Specification / Analysis; analysis measured at KIT)

materials.notes: Text of Table 3 read directly from the PDF. This is a 2026 paper reproducing the EUROFER97-3 specification, not the original Lindau et al., Fusion Eng. Des. 75-79 (2005) 989 or the ENEA/KIT 'Chemical specification of EUROFER 97' (not retrieved). Fe 'not defined' in the spec; balance. Odd: spec O max 0.01 vs measured 0.0004. A EUROfusion preprint (Testani et al., WPMAT-CPR(18)18575) states Ni, Mo, Cu, Nb, Al, B, Co 'as low as possible (ALAP)' and As+Sn+Sb+Zr ~0.05 total (not itemised). Density could not be verified from a primary source; ~7.8 g/cm3 is the commonly quoted RT value (unverified here).

materials.name: SS316L(N)-IG (ITER grade)

impurity_limits_wt_percent.B: 0.0010 (IAEA FEC 2025 table) vs 0.0020 (ITER plate spec, Russian-language IDM copy)

materials.nominal_choice_note: Majors at range midpoints; C, Si, P, S are max-only so I suggest ~50-60% of max (same convention as PNNL). For activation use Co 0.05, Ta 0.01 (agreed by both sources) and the CONSERVATIVE Nb 0.10 and B 0.0010 unless the user chooses otherwise; sources disagree on Nb and B.

source.citation: (a) S.W. Kim et al. (KFE), IAEA FEC 2025 paper/synopsis on SS316L(N)-IG, Table 1 (https://conferences.iaea.org/event/392/papers/36393/); (b) ITER specification for 316L(N)-IG hot-rolled plate 5-100 mm (Word doc mirrored at a-k-d.ru, document no./version not legible), citing RCC-MR 2007 RM 3321
source.table: (a) Table 1; (b) chemical composition table

materials.notes: The primary ITER Materials Properties Handbook / IDM procurement spec was not accessed. (a) was reported through a search summary only (direct fetch returned 403); (b) was text-recovered from a corrupted .doc binary. Both agree on all majors, Cu 0.30, Co 0.05, Ta 0.01, Ti 0.10; they disagree on Nb (0.10 vs 0.01) and B (0.0010 vs 0.0020). ITER nuclear analysis separately cites Co<=0.05, Nb<=0.1, Ta<=0.05 inside cryostat (Barabash-type statement, secondary). Do not treat as final until the ITER_D spec is checked.

materials.name: Pb-15.7Li eutectic (natural Li)
materials.density_hint_unverified: 9.88 g/cm3 at 573 K (300 C) from correlation below; solid at room T
materials.density_correlation: rho[kg/m3] = 10581.8 - 1.229*T[K], valid 508-997 K (Khairulin, as recommended in Favuzza 2024); gives 9.88 g/cm3 at 573 K and 9.84 g/cm3 at 600 K
materials.nominal_choice_note: CRITICAL: '15.7' is ATOM percent Li (Pb84.3Li15.7). Weight fractions computed here: Li 15.7*6.941/(15.7*6.941+84.3*207.2) = 0.6200 wt%, Pb 99.380 wt%. Natural Li isotopics (7.5% Li-6) assumed; no enrichment. Impurity limits (e.g. Bi, Ag, Fe) not found.

source.citation: P. Favuzza, 'Chemistry and relevant thermophysical properties of Pb84.3Li15.7 liquid solutions: Updated view and identification of new and coherent values', Results in Materials 23 (2024) 100622, DOI 10.1016/j.rinma.2024.100622
source.table: Eq. (20) / Table 4 (density correlations, Khairulin 15.7 at.% Li)

materials.notes: Density correlation read directly from paper text. Mas de les Valls et al., J. Nucl. Mater. 376 (2008) 353 is the other standard reference (not retrieved).
